facts.fact: Nielsen's The Gauge reports that streaming accounted for 47.6% of all U.S. TV viewing in April 2026.
facts.quote: In April 2026, the most recent month measured, streaming took 47.6% of all U.S. TV viewing, while cable held just 21.6% and broadcast 19.9%, according to Nielsen.

facts.fact: Nielsen's The Gauge reports that cable accounted for 21.6% of all U.S. TV viewing in April 2026.

facts.fact: Nielsen's The Gauge reports that YouTube held 13.4% of all U.S. TV viewing in April 2026, the most of any single service.
facts.quote: YouTube held 13.4% of all U.S. TV viewing in April 2026, making it the single most-watched service on American television

facts.fact: Nielsen's The Gauge reports that Netflix was the second most-watched individual service with 7.8% of U.S. TV viewing in April 2026.

facts.fact: According to Nielsen's The Gauge, no other single streaming service held more than 5% of U.S. TV viewing in April 2026.

facts.fact: eMarketer estimates that in 2026 about 80.7 million U.S. households have cut the cord or never had cable.

facts.fact: eMarketer estimates that cord-cut or cord-never households outnumber pay-TV households by more than 25 million in 2026.

facts.fact: According to eMarketer, traditional pay-TV reaches only around 42% of U.S. households in 2026.
facts.quote: Traditional pay-TV now reaches only around 42% of households, down from roughly 88% in 2010.
